entities.name: Methyl ester saponification
observations: The reactant methyl aromatic carboxylate is converted to the corresponding free carboxylic acid by cleavage of the acyl–O–CH3 ester bond.
The matched empirical condition uses sodium hydroxide in methanol, followed by protonation during workup.
No new carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, or ring bonds are formed; the amide and tertiary amine remain unchanged.

entities.name: NaOH in methanol
observations: Sodium hydroxide in methanol is the matched reagent system for hydrolyzing the methyl ester to the carboxylic acid.
Aqueous or mixed methanol/water hydroxide and acidic aqueous workup are plausible operational variants.

entities.name: Sodium hydroxide
observations: Base reagent for saponification of the methyl ester in the supplied reaction.

entities.name: Methanol
observations: Solvent used with sodium hydroxide in the matched ester-hydrolysis reaction.

entities.name: Acidic aqueous workup
observations: Protonation/workup step converts the carboxylate intermediate into the isolated carboxylic acid.
